pins.why: Read word for word, this row's plan moves L2 ('records → rows') to Rust at its native step (DESIGN-V5 4 and 11), and in TypeScript lets the kernel own the rows while the main thread projects only the rows it reads (DESIGN-V5 11, decision 13). On the strict DATA-01 reading that would put the rows of record in a second engine, SRV's shape. The pin keeps data the engine on every full replica in every phase. It is a rule the row may carry: REQUIREMENTS X3 names it as one of the two ways out of the clash; E-03 measured the crossing (under 1 ns a record at batch 256); RUST runs this split and both judges met its DATA-09; E-05 priced a full projection beside the worker's copy at 510 to 528 B a small row, under DEP-13's 2 KB, and found the worker's digest equal to the main thread's; E-34 woke 5.1 GB of 2 KB rows in that form. It adds no mechanism (the seam is A-30's, which the row already takes) and moves no counted cell but DATA-09. Its price: memory, since a full replica holds every row in data as well as whatever the worker keeps (E-34 could not run 10 GB of 2 KB rows in the two-copy form on its 16 GB box: about twice the heap; an index without the values halves that); and the native step does not speed up the fold (data's lane folds at 0.22 to 1.90 us a record, E-05). No settled cell of this row credits a native fold or a single copy: SC-05 (10 GB) is open on its own reasons, and DEP-13 on the empty copy. If a later timing shows L2 must go native, the row drops the pin, DATA-09 goes back to open, and on the strict reading the row then fails as SRV does.

This row keeps learners. record_fixes.to: A replica that finds a damaged entry by its checksum marks it bad. It keeps its id and its place as a voter, but while an entry is marked it grants no vote, takes no append and does not stand, and it neither serves nor folds past the bad entry (a reader asking for that position gets END, A-06). It copies the entry from any peer whose own copy is not marked and whose commit index covers it, then clears the mark. A damaged entry above the replica's own commit point needs PAR's 'possibly committed' query, which was not modelled (G-15).
record_fixes.why: E-37's 7 checked rules, each shown needed. 'Keeps its vote' as written loses a committed write (the vote mutant broke MoreUpToDateCorrectInv in 32 states), and F-22 (M) asks that the replica never votes or acknowledges on the bad entry. The read-path sentence is j2's: a damaged replica must not hand its zeroed record to a reader, relay or fold.

E-37's ZTimeout guard: a damaged replica does not stand. Dropping it broke LogMatchingInv on par2d in 56 states. Standing is this unit's rule (the election timer and the pre-vote), so it reads the mark. +1 pair, with par-repair.
